ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.24741v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disease in the world, and 70\% to 75\% of PD patients suffer from speech disorders at some stage. Since PD affects men more frequently than women, previous publications tend to rely on unbalanced datasets that potentially introduce sex biases into trained models. This study investigates sex differences in PD detection from speech using deep learning and traditional machine learning approaches. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.23348v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Clinical interviews are central to depression assessment but time-consuming and rater-dependent. Automated severity estimation offers scalable screening, yet existing methods often retain interviewer speech (confounding participant cues), fuse modalities late (losing fine-grained cross-modal dynamics), or score symptoms independently (ignoring inter-symptom correlations). ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.23847v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Audio artificial intelligence (AI) now recognizes speech, sounds, and music remarkably well, yet voice agents still act when they should not: they execute commands addressed to others, act on misheard content, and commit before the user finishes speaking. This position article argues that the bottleneck in agentic audio AI has shifted from recognition to decision-making. Abstract: We present a novel approach to the problem of combining two voice-line channels of dyadic conversational audio into a unified conversation with controllable back-channeling and turn-taking dynamics. Abstract: Prior work on engagement modeling in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has demonstrated substantial individual variability in behavioral features, particularly in visual modalities.
